full_judgment: 12. If a court has no jurisdiction to try a suit, it goes to very root of the matter and it is a case of inherent lack of jurisdiction. Preponderance principle is that the jurisdiction of a civil court to deal with civil causes can be excluded by a special law to deal with special subject-matters. It is only if the said law must expressly provide for such exclusion. The presumption to be drawn must be in favour of the existence rather than exclusion of the jurisdiction. The test aiming such question is (a) whether the legislature intent to exclude arises explicitly and (b) whether the statute provides for adequate and satisfactory alternative remedy to a party aggrieved by an order made under it. Exclusion of jurisdiction of civil court is not readily to be inferred unless law regarding exclusion of jurisdiction has been laid down. (State of Andra Pradesh vs Manjeti Laxmi Kantha Rao, AIR 2000 SC 2220, Secy of State vs Mask, AIR 1940 PC 105; Church of North India vs Lavajibhai Ratanjibhai, AIR 2005 SC 2544).
